titleStmt.title: Diplomatic transcription of MS Jaipur RORI 6838: 03 Śārīrasthānam 4

msIdentifier.idno: RORI Catalogue, vol. XI, serial no. 3988

msContents.summary: An incomplete manuscript transmitting portions of the Suśrutasaṃhitā together with Gayadāsa’s Nyāyacandrikā. The extant portion covers Sūtrasthāna 18-46, Nidānasthāna 1-16, and Śārīrasthāna 1-10.

physDesc.p: The extant physical bundle comprises approximately 560 folios. The digital copy contains 1,115 photographs of individual folio sides.

supportDesc.foliation: The principal foliation is written in the lower part of the right margin of each verso. The Nidānasthāna and Śārīrasthāna also have separate sectional foliations, each beginning with 1. The opening folios 1-215 are missing. Folio 287 occurs twice. The foliation of folios 656-665 is no longer visible because the right margins have broken away.
supportDesc.condition: The manuscript is incomplete and partly damaged. Most damage is confined to the margins. A large wormhole affects the right side of folios 426-547 and, at its largest, crosses seven lines and extends across approximately seven or eight akṣaras.

layoutDesc.layout: Each side contains ten lines, with approximately 40-45 akṣaras per line. Straight orange-red lines mark the left and right boundaries of the writing area.

handDesc.handNote: The manuscript is written in a clear variety of Devanagari.

decoDesc.decoNote: Each verso has an orange-red circle in both margins, occasionally elaborated into a floral design.

The manuscript is extensively rubricated in orange-red ink. Rubrication is used for, among other things, colophons, phrases introducing citations, and the syllable cha marking the beginning of a passage from the mūla.

origin.origDate: Vikrama Saṃvat 1525, bright half of Bhādrapada, seventh tithi, Sunday: 6 September 1467 in the Julian calendar, corresponding to 15 September 1467 in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.
origin.p: The manuscript was copied during the reign of Sultan Maḥmūd I Begadā. It was commissioned by Minister Śrī Māṇḍaṇa, son of the physician and minister Śrī Nārāyaṇa, for the study of his sons and grandsons. The scribe identifies himself as Rāula Nārasiṃha. Both the commissioner and the scribe belonged to the Ābhyantara Nāgara community.

adminInfo.note: RORI 6838 and RORI 5157 preserve different surviving portions of the same original manuscript. RORI 5157 contains the Kalpasthāna. The intervening Cikitsāsthāna and the subsequent Uttaratantra have not yet been located.

revisionDesc.change: Added transcription of SS and NC 3.4.81-99.
